questions.question: Which keyword declares a variable that can be reassigned?
questions.explanation: The let keyword declares a variable whose value can be reassigned.

questions.question: Complete the code: ______ name = "Alex";
questions.explanation: The let keyword declares a variable that can later be reassigned.

questions.question: Which keyword is used for a value that should not be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const creates a binding that cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: Complete the code: ______ score = 100;
questions.explanation: const is appropriate when the variable should not be reassigned.

questions.question: What is the value of x after this code? let x = 5; x = 8;
questions.explanation: The second assignment changes x from 5 to 8.

flashcards.title: Variable
flashcards.definition: A named place used to store a value.

flashcards.title: let
flashcards.definition: Declares a variable that can be reassigned.

flashcards.title: const
flashcards.definition: Declares a binding that cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: What is printed by this code? let count = 2; count += 3; console.log(count);
questions.explanation: The += operator adds 3 to the current value of count, producing 5.

questions.question: Complete the code to declare a block-scoped variable: ______ message = "Hi";
questions.explanation: let creates a block-scoped variable.

questions.question: What happens when you execute const x = 5; x = 10;?
questions.explanation: A const binding cannot be reassigned, so the assignment causes a TypeError.

questions.question: Complete the code: let points = 10; points ______ 5;
questions.explanation: The += assignment operator adds the right-hand value to the existing variable.

questions.question: Which declaration is block-scoped?
questions.explanation: Both let and const are block-scoped declarations.

flashcards.title: Reassignment
flashcards.definition: Changing the value stored in a variable.

flashcards.title: Compound Assignment
flashcards.definition: An operator that updates a variable using its current value.

flashcards.title: Block Scope
flashcards.definition: Scope limited to the block where a declaration is created.

questions.question: What is printed? const user = { name: "Mia" }; user.name = "Leo"; console.log(user.name);
questions.explanation: const prevents reassignment of the object binding, but object properties can still be changed.

questions.question: Complete the declaration: ______ settings = { theme: "dark" };
questions.explanation: const is commonly used when the object reference itself should not be reassigned.

questions.question: Which statement about var is correct?
questions.explanation: Variables declared with var are function-scoped rather than block-scoped.

questions.question: Complete the code: const total = price * ______;
questions.explanation: The expression multiplies the price by the quantity variable.

questions.question: What is the main difference between let and const?
choices: let can be reassigned while const cannot
questions.explanation: The important distinction is that a let binding may be reassigned while a const binding may not.

flashcards.title: var
flashcards.definition: An older JavaScript variable declaration that is function-scoped.

flashcards.title: Constant Object
flashcards.definition: An object whose variable binding cannot be reassigned.

flashcards.title: Destructuring Declaration
flashcards.definition: A declaration that extracts values from an object or array.

questions.question: Which data type represents text?
questions.explanation: A string represents text such as "Hello".

questions.question: Complete the code: let name = ______;
questions.explanation: Text values in JavaScript can be written as strings using quotation marks.

questions.question: Which value is a Boolean?
questions.explanation: true without quotation marks is a Boolean value.

questions.question: Complete the code: let age = ______;
questions.explanation: 20 is a numeric literal.

questions.question: Which value represents the absence of an intentional value?
questions.explanation: null is commonly used to explicitly represent no value.

flashcards.title: String
flashcards.definition: A sequence of text characters.

flashcards.title: Number
flashcards.definition: A numeric value, including integers and decimals.

flashcards.title: Boolean
flashcards.definition: A value that is either true or false.

questions.question: What is the type of the value returned by typeof "hello"?
questions.explanation: typeof returns "string" for string values.

questions.question: Complete the expression: typeof ______
questions.explanation: The typeof operator can be used to inspect the type of a value.

questions.question: What does typeof null return in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: JavaScript has a historical behavior where typeof null returns "object".

questions.question: Complete the code to create an undefined variable: let value = ______;
questions.explanation: undefined is the JavaScript value representing an uninitialized or missing value.

questions.question: What is the result of Number("25")?
questions.explanation: Number converts the numeric string "25" into the number 25.

flashcards.title: typeof
flashcards.definition: An operator that returns a string describing a value's type.

flashcards.title: undefined
flashcards.definition: A value commonly used when no value has been assigned.

flashcards.title: NaN
flashcards.definition: A special numeric value meaning Not-a-Number.

questions.question: What is the result of Number("10") + 5?
questions.explanation: Number converts "10" to 10, so 10 + 5 produces 15.

questions.question: Complete the conversion: ______("123")
questions.explanation: Number converts a value into a numeric value when possible.

questions.question: What is the result of String(42)?
questions.explanation: String(42) returns the string "42".

questions.question: Complete the conversion: ______(true)
questions.explanation: String(true) converts the Boolean value into the string "true".

questions.question: Which value is falsy in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: The number 0 is falsy. Non-empty strings and objects are truthy.

flashcards.title: Type Conversion
flashcards.definition: Changing a value from one data type to another.

flashcards.title: Truthy
flashcards.definition: A value that behaves like true in a Boolean context.

flashcards.title: Falsy
flashcards.definition: A value that behaves like false in a Boolean context.

questions.question: Which operator adds two numbers?
questions.explanation: The + operator performs addition when used with numbers.

questions.question: Complete the expression: 8 ______ 2
questions.explanation: The + operator adds the two operands.

questions.question: What is 10 % 3?
questions.explanation: The remainder after dividing 10 by 3 is 1.

questions.question: Complete the multiplication expression: 4 ______ 5
questions.explanation: The * operator performs multiplication.

questions.question: Which operator performs division?
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses / for division.

flashcards.title: Arithmetic Operator
flashcards.definition: An operator used to perform mathematical calculations.

flashcards.title: Addition
flashcards.definition: Combines two numeric values.

flashcards.title: Remainder
flashcards.definition: The value left after integer division.

questions.question: Which operator checks strict equality?
questions.explanation: === checks equality of both value and type without type coercion.

questions.question: Complete the comparison: age ______ 18
questions.explanation: >= checks whether age is greater than or equal to 18.

questions.question: What is the result of 5 > 3?
questions.explanation: 5 is greater than 3, so the comparison evaluates to true.

questions.question: Complete the logical expression: isMember ______ hasTicket
questions.explanation: The && operator requires both Boolean expressions to be true.

questions.question: What does the ! operator do?
questions.explanation: The ! operator logically negates a value.

flashcards.title: Strict Equality
flashcards.definition: Compares both value and type.

flashcards.title: Logical AND
flashcards.definition: Returns true when both conditions are true.

flashcards.title: Logical NOT
flashcards.definition: Reverses a Boolean value.

questions.question: What is the result of 2 + 3 * 4?
questions.explanation: Multiplication has higher precedence, so 3 * 4 is evaluated before adding 2.

questions.question: Complete the expression to use the conditional operator: age >= 18 ______ "adult" : "minor"
questions.explanation: The ? begins the true branch of a ternary conditional expression.

questions.question: What is the result of 5 === "5"?
questions.explanation: The values have different types, so strict equality returns false.

questions.question: Complete the expression: result = score > 50 ______ "pass" : "fail";
questions.explanation: The ternary operator uses ? to specify the expression for a true condition.

questions.question: Which operator returns the right-hand value when the left-hand value is null or undefined?
questions.explanation: The nullish coalescing operator ?? checks specifically for null or undefined.

flashcards.title: Operator Precedence
flashcards.definition: Rules that determine which operators are evaluated first.

flashcards.title: Ternary Operator
flashcards.definition: A compact way to choose between two expressions.

flashcards.title: Nullish Coalescing
flashcards.definition: Provides a fallback only for null or undefined.

questions.question: Which keyword begins a conditional statement?
questions.explanation: The if keyword begins a conditional statement.

questions.question: Complete the code: ______ (age >= 18) { console.log("Adult"); }
questions.explanation: if executes its block when the condition is true.

questions.question: Which keyword provides an alternative when an if condition is false?
questions.explanation: The else block runs when the preceding if condition is false.

questions.question: Complete the code: if (score >= 50) { pass(); } ______ { fail(); }
questions.explanation: else provides the alternative branch.

questions.question: What happens if an if condition is false and there is no else?
questions.explanation: When the condition is false, JavaScript skips the if block.

flashcards.title: if
flashcards.definition: Runs a block when a condition is true.

flashcards.title: else
flashcards.definition: Runs a block when an if condition is false.

flashcards.title: Condition
flashcards.definition: An expression that evaluates to true or false.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to test another condition after if?
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses else if for additional conditions.

questions.question: Complete the code: if (score >= 90) { grade = "A"; } ______ (score >= 80) { grade = "B"; }
questions.explanation: else if adds another condition to a conditional chain.

questions.question: What is printed if x = 7? if (x > 10) console.log("A"); else if (x > 5) console.log("B"); else console.log("C");
questions.explanation: 7 is not greater than 10 but is greater than 5, so B is printed.

questions.question: Complete the condition: if (age >= 13 ______ age <= 19) { teen = true; }
questions.explanation: Both age conditions must be true, so logical AND is appropriate.

questions.question: Which structure is best for checking several possible values of one expression?
questions.explanation: switch is designed for comparing one expression against multiple cases.

flashcards.title: else if
flashcards.definition: Tests another condition when previous conditions are false.

flashcards.title: Nested Condition
flashcards.definition: A conditional statement placed inside another conditional block.

flashcards.title: switch
flashcards.definition: Selects a block based on matching cases.

questions.question: What does the default clause in a switch statement do?
questions.explanation: default provides code to execute when none of the cases match.

questions.question: Complete the switch statement: switch (day) { case 1: console.log("Mon"); ______; }
questions.explanation: break exits the switch after the matching case executes.

questions.question: What is printed by true && false || true?
questions.explanation: && is evaluated first: true && false is false, then false || true is true.

questions.question: Complete the guarded condition: if (user && user.isAdmin) { ______ }
questions.explanation: The function call represents an action performed when both conditions are truthy.

questions.question: Which operator is useful for selecting a fallback when a value is falsy?
questions.explanation: The logical OR operator can provide a fallback for falsy values.

flashcards.title: default
flashcards.definition: The switch branch used when no case matches.

flashcards.title: break
flashcards.definition: Stops execution of the current switch or loop.

flashcards.title: Short-Circuit Evaluation
flashcards.definition: Logical operators can stop evaluating once the result is known.

questions.question: Which loop is commonly used when the number of iterations is known?
questions.explanation: A for loop is commonly used when initialization, condition, and update can be defined.

questions.question: Complete the loop: ______ (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) { console.log(i); }
questions.explanation: for introduces a standard counter-controlled loop.

questions.question: How many times does for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) execute?
questions.explanation: The loop runs for i values 0, 1, and 2, for three iterations.

questions.question: Complete the update expression: for (let i = 0; i < 5; i______)
questions.explanation: ++ increases i by one after each iteration.

questions.question: Which keyword immediately exits a loop?
questions.explanation: break immediately exits the nearest loop.

flashcards.title: for Loop
flashcards.definition: A loop with initialization, condition, and update expressions.

flashcards.title: Iteration
flashcards.definition: One execution of a loop body.

flashcards.title: break
flashcards.definition: Stops the nearest loop immediately.

questions.question: Which loop continues while a condition remains true?
questions.explanation: A while loop repeatedly executes while its condition is true.

questions.question: Complete the loop: ______ (count > 0) { count--; }
questions.explanation: while evaluates the condition before each iteration.

questions.question: What does continue do inside a loop?
questions.explanation: continue skips the remaining body of the current iteration and proceeds to the next one.

questions.question: Complete the statement to skip an iteration: ______;
questions.explanation: continue skips the rest of the current loop iteration.

questions.question: Which loop always executes its body at least once?
questions.explanation: A do...while loop executes its body before checking the condition.

flashcards.title: while Loop
flashcards.definition: Repeats while its condition is true.

flashcards.title: continue
flashcards.definition: Skips the remainder of the current loop iteration.

flashcards.title: do...while
flashcards.definition: A loop that executes its body before checking the condition.

questions.question: Which loop is designed to iterate over iterable values such as array elements?
questions.explanation: for...of iterates over values produced by an iterable.

questions.question: Complete the loop: for (const item ______ items) { console.log(item); }
questions.explanation: for...of uses of to iterate through iterable values.

questions.question: What does for...in primarily iterate over for an object?
questions.explanation: for...in iterates over enumerable property keys.

questions.question: Complete the nested loop: for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { for (let j = 0; j < 2; ______) { } }
questions.explanation: The inner loop increments j on each iteration.

questions.question: What is the main risk of a while loop whose condition never becomes false?
questions.explanation: A condition that remains true can cause the loop to execute indefinitely.

flashcards.title: for...of
flashcards.definition: Iterates over values from an iterable.

flashcards.title: for...in
flashcards.definition: Iterates over enumerable property keys.

flashcards.title: Nested Loop
flashcards.definition: A loop placed inside another loop.

questions.question: Which keyword declares a function?
questions.explanation: JavaScript uses the function keyword for function declarations.

questions.question: Complete the declaration: ______ greet() { console.log("Hello"); }
questions.explanation: function begins a standard function declaration.

questions.question: How do you call a function named greet?
questions.explanation: Parentheses invoke the function.

questions.question: Complete the call: calculate______
questions.explanation: Arguments are passed inside parentheses when a function is called.

questions.question: What is a parameter?
choices: A value returned by a function
A named input in a function definition
questions.explanation: A parameter is a named variable in a function definition that receives an argument.

flashcards.title: Function
flashcards.definition: A reusable block of code that performs a task.

flashcards.title: Parameter
flashcards.definition: A named input defined by a function.

flashcards.title: Argument
flashcards.definition: A value supplied when calling a function.

questions.question: Which keyword sends a value back from a function?
questions.explanation: return ends a function and can provide a value to the caller.

questions.question: Complete the function: function add(a, b) { ______ a + b; }
questions.explanation: return sends the sum back to the caller.

questions.question: What does this return? function double(x) { return x * 2; } double(4);
questions.explanation: The function multiplies 4 by 2, returning 8.

questions.question: Complete the arrow function: const square = x ______ x * x;
questions.explanation: The arrow syntax uses => to define an arrow function.

questions.question: Which syntax creates an arrow function with one parameter?
questions.explanation: x => x * 2 is a valid arrow function.

flashcards.title: return
flashcards.definition: Ends a function and optionally provides a value.

flashcards.title: Arrow Function
flashcards.definition: A compact syntax for defining functions.

flashcards.title: Default Parameter
flashcards.definition: A parameter value used when no argument is supplied.

questions.question: What is returned by function add(a, b = 2) { return a + b; } when called as add(3)?
questions.explanation: b uses its default value of 2, so 3 + 2 returns 5.

questions.question: Complete the default parameter: function greet(name = ______) { return name; }
questions.explanation: The string Guest is used when no name argument is supplied.

questions.question: What does a function passed into another function represent?
questions.explanation: A function passed to another function is commonly called a callback.

questions.question: Complete the callback call: numbers.forEach(______)
questions.explanation: console.log can be passed as a callback to forEach to process each value.

questions.question: Which statement about functions in JavaScript is true?
choices: Functions cannot be stored in variables
Functions can be passed as values
questions.explanation: JavaScript functions are first-class values and can be stored, passed, and returned.

flashcards.title: Callback
flashcards.definition: A function passed to another function to be called later.

flashcards.title: Higher-Order Function
flashcards.definition: A function that accepts or returns another function.

flashcards.title: Function Expression
flashcards.definition: A function assigned to a variable or another expression.

questions.question: Which syntax creates an array?
questions.explanation: Square brackets create an array literal.

questions.question: Complete the array: const colors = ______;
questions.explanation: Array elements are written inside square brackets and separated by commas.

questions.question: What is the index of the first array element?
questions.explanation: JavaScript arrays use zero-based indexing.

questions.question: Complete the expression to access the first item: colors[______]
questions.explanation: Index 0 refers to the first element.

questions.question: Which property gives the number of elements in an array?
questions.explanation: The length property gives the number of elements.

flashcards.title: Array
flashcards.definition: An ordered collection of values.

flashcards.title: Index
flashcards.definition: A numeric position used to access an array element.

flashcards.title: length
flashcards.definition: The number of elements currently in an array.

questions.question: Which method adds an element to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: push adds one or more elements to the end of an array.

questions.question: Complete the method call: numbers.______(10);
questions.explanation: push appends the value 10 to the end of the array.

questions.question: Which method removes the last array element?
questions.explanation: pop removes and returns the last array element.

questions.question: Complete the method call that removes the first element: numbers.______();
questions.explanation: shift removes and returns the first array element.

questions.question: What does push return?
questions.explanation: push returns the new length of the array.

flashcards.title: push
flashcards.definition: Adds elements to the end of an array.

flashcards.title: pop
flashcards.definition: Removes and returns the last array element.

flashcards.title: shift
flashcards.definition: Removes and returns the first array element.

questions.question: Which array method creates a new array containing elements that pass a condition?
questions.explanation: filter creates a new array containing elements for which the callback returns true.

questions.question: Complete the transformation: numbers.______(n => n * 2);
questions.explanation: map creates a new array by transforming each element.

questions.question: What does reduce commonly do?
choices: Combines array values into one result
questions.explanation: reduce processes elements and accumulates them into a single result.

questions.question: Complete the search: users.______(user => user.id === 5);
questions.explanation: find returns the first element that satisfies the condition.

questions.question: Which method returns a new array without changing the original array?
questions.explanation: map creates a new array from the callback results.

flashcards.title: map
flashcards.definition: Creates a new array by transforming each element.

flashcards.title: filter
flashcards.definition: Creates a new array containing elements that pass a test.

flashcards.title: reduce
flashcards.definition: Combines array elements into an accumulated result.

questions.question: Which syntax creates an object literal?
questions.explanation: Curly braces create an object literal.

questions.question: Complete the object: const user = ______ name: "Ana" };
questions.explanation: An object literal begins with an opening curly brace.

questions.question: How do you access the name property of user?
questions.explanation: Dot notation accesses an object property by its identifier.

questions.question: Complete the access: user.______
questions.explanation: name is the property being accessed.

questions.question: What does an object primarily store?
questions.explanation: JavaScript objects store properties as key-value pairs.

flashcards.title: Object
flashcards.definition: A collection of named properties and values.

flashcards.title: Property
flashcards.definition: A named value stored inside an object.

flashcards.title: Dot Notation
flashcards.definition: A way to access an object property using a dot.

questions.question: Which notation allows a property name to come from a variable?
questions.explanation: Bracket notation evaluates the expression inside the brackets to determine the property key.

questions.question: Complete the access using a variable key: user[______]
questions.explanation: Bracket notation uses the value of key to select the property.

questions.question: What happens when assigning user.age = 20 to an object without an age property?
questions.explanation: Assigning a new property adds that property to the object.

questions.question: Complete the method definition: const user = { greet() { ______ "Hi"; } };
questions.explanation: return sends the string from the object method.

questions.question: Which built-in method returns an array of an object's property names?
questions.explanation: Object.keys returns an array containing enumerable own property names.

flashcards.title: Bracket Notation
flashcards.definition: Accesses a property using an expression inside brackets.

flashcards.title: Object Method
flashcards.definition: A function stored as an object property.

flashcards.title: Object.keys
flashcards.definition: Returns an array of an object's enumerable property names.

questions.question: What does object destructuring allow you to do?
questions.explanation: Destructuring extracts selected object properties into variables.

questions.question: Complete the destructuring: const { ______ } = user;
questions.explanation: name is extracted from the user object.

questions.question: What does the spread syntax {...user, active: true} create?
choices: A new object with copied properties plus active
questions.explanation: Object spread copies enumerable properties into a new object literal.

questions.question: Complete the object spread: const copy = { ______user };
questions.explanation: The ... syntax spreads properties from user into the new object.

questions.question: Which method returns an array containing an object's key-value pairs as arrays?
questions.explanation: Object.entries returns an array of [key, value] pairs.

flashcards.title: Object Destructuring
flashcards.definition: Extracts selected properties from an object.

flashcards.title: Object Spread
flashcards.definition: Copies enumerable properties into another object.

flashcards.title: Object.entries
flashcards.definition: Returns key-value pairs from an object.

questions.question: What does scope determine?
choices: Where a variable can be accessed
questions.explanation: Scope determines where variables and other identifiers are accessible.

questions.question: Complete the block-scoped declaration: { ______ value = 10; }
questions.explanation: let creates a block-scoped variable.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to manually create an error?
questions.explanation: throw raises an exception in JavaScript.

questions.question: Complete the statement: ______ new Error("Invalid input");
questions.explanation: throw raises the Error object as an exception.

questions.question: Which block is commonly used to handle an exception?
questions.explanation: catch handles an exception thrown by the associated try block.

flashcards.title: Scope
flashcards.definition: The region where an identifier can be accessed.

flashcards.title: throw
flashcards.definition: Raises an exception manually.

flashcards.title: catch
flashcards.definition: Handles an exception from a try block.

questions.question: Which keyword begins code that may throw an exception?
questions.explanation: A try block contains code that can be handled by catch.

questions.question: Complete the error handler: try { riskyOperation(); } ______ (error) { console.log(error); }
questions.explanation: catch receives an exception thrown by the try block.

questions.question: What does finally do?
choices: Runs only when an error occurs
Runs only when no error occurs
Runs after try/catch regardless of the outcome
questions.explanation: finally normally runs after try and catch processing regardless of whether an exception occurred.

questions.question: Complete the structure: try { work(); } catch (e) { handle(e); } ______ { cleanup(); }
questions.explanation: finally is used for cleanup that should occur after the try/catch process.

questions.question: What happens to a let variable declared inside an if block after the block ends?
choices: It is not accessible outside the block
questions.explanation: let variables are block-scoped.

flashcards.title: try
flashcards.definition: Contains code whose exceptions can be handled.

flashcards.title: finally
flashcards.definition: Contains cleanup code that runs after exception handling.

flashcards.title: Block Scope
flashcards.definition: Limits let and const identifiers to their surrounding block.

questions.question: What happens when an exception is thrown and no matching catch handles it?
choices: It propagates to the caller or environment
questions.explanation: An unhandled exception propagates through the call stack until handled or reported by the environment.

questions.question: Complete the custom error: throw new ______("Invalid score");
questions.explanation: Error creates a standard JavaScript error object.

questions.question: Which scope is created by a function declaration?
questions.explanation: Functions create their own function execution scope.

questions.question: Complete the closure example: function outer() { let count = 0; return function() { return ______; }; }
questions.explanation: The inner function can access count from the surrounding lexical scope, forming a closure.

questions.question: What is a closure?
choices: A function retaining access to its lexical environment
questions.explanation: A closure occurs when a function retains access to variables from its surrounding lexical scope.

flashcards.title: Closure
flashcards.definition: A function that retains access to its surrounding lexical environment.
flashcards.syntax: function outer() { let x = 1; return () => x; }

flashcards.title: Exception Propagation
flashcards.definition: The movement of an unhandled exception up the call stack.

flashcards.title: Lexical Scope
flashcards.definition: Scope determined by where code is written.

questions.question: Which type stores whole numbers such as 25?
questions.explanation: int stores integer values without a fractional part.

questions.question: Complete the declaration: ______ age = 20;
questions.explanation: int is the Java primitive type used for whole-number values.

questions.question: Which Java type stores text?
questions.explanation: String represents a sequence of characters.

questions.question: Complete the declaration: String ______ = "Alex";
questions.explanation: name is the variable identifier storing the String value.

questions.question: Which type stores true or false?
questions.explanation: boolean stores either true or false.

flashcards.title: int
flashcards.definition: A primitive type for whole numbers.

flashcards.title: String
flashcards.definition: A class used to represent text.

flashcards.title: boolean
flashcards.definition: A primitive type containing true or false.

questions.question: Which type is commonly used for decimal values such as 3.14?
questions.explanation: double stores double-precision floating-point values.

questions.question: Complete the declaration: ______ price = 19.99;
questions.explanation: double is suitable for decimal floating-point values.

questions.question: Which keyword creates a variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: A final variable cannot be assigned a new value after initialization.

questions.question: Complete the declaration: ______ int MAX = 100;
questions.explanation: final prevents the variable from being reassigned.

questions.question: Which primitive type stores a single character?
questions.explanation: char stores a single UTF-16 code unit and uses single quotes for literals.

flashcards.title: double
flashcards.definition: A primitive type for double-precision decimal values.

flashcards.title: final
flashcards.definition: Prevents a variable from being reassigned.

flashcards.title: char
flashcards.definition: A primitive type for a single character.

questions.question: Which type is generally the widest primitive integer type?
questions.explanation: long provides a wider integer range than byte, short, and int.

questions.question: Complete the declaration for a long literal: long distance = 5000000000______;
questions.explanation: The L suffix marks the integer literal as a long.

questions.question: What is the result type of 5 / 2 when both operands are int?
questions.explanation: Integer division produces an int result, so 5 / 2 evaluates to 2.

questions.question: Complete the cast: double result = (double) ______ / 2;
questions.explanation: Casting 5 to double makes the division produce a decimal result.

questions.question: Which type is used for a single Unicode code unit in Java?
questions.explanation: char represents a UTF-16 code unit.

flashcards.title: long
flashcards.definition: A primitive integer type with a wider range than int.

flashcards.title: Type Casting
flashcards.definition: Explicitly converting a value to another compatible type.

flashcards.title: Integer Division
flashcards.definition: Division of integers that discards the fractional part.

questions.question: Which operator performs addition?
questions.explanation: The + operator adds numeric operands.

questions.question: Complete the expression: int total = 5 ______ 3;
questions.explanation: The + operator performs addition.

questions.question: What is 10 % 3?

questions.question: Why can getline appear to read an empty line after std::cin >> value?

questions.question: Complete the condition: if (std::cin.______()) { std::cerr << "Invalid"; }
questions.explanation: fail() indicates that a formatted input operation failed.

questions.question: Which stream is conventionally used for error messages?
questions.explanation: std::cerr is the standard error output stream.

flashcards.title: std::ignore

flashcards.title: fail

flashcards.title: std::cerr

questions.question: Which keyword begins a conditional statement?
questions.explanation: if begins a conditional statement.

questions.question: Complete the statement: ______ (age >= 18) { std::cout << "Adult"; }
questions.explanation: if runs the block when its condition is true.

questions.question: Which keyword provides an alternative branch?
questions.explanation: else runs when the preceding if condition is false.

questions.question: Complete the branch: if (x > 0) { } ______ { }
questions.explanation: else defines the alternative branch.

questions.question: What happens when an if condition is false and there is no else?
questions.explanation: The body of a false if statement is skipped.

flashcards.title: if
flashcards.definition: Runs code when a condition is true.

flashcards.title: else
flashcards.definition: Runs code when the if condition is false.

flashcards.title: Condition
flashcards.definition: An expression used to decide which code runs.

questions.question: Which keyword tests another condition after if?
questions.explanation: C++ uses else if for additional conditions.

questions.question: Complete the code: if (score >= 90) { } ______ (score >= 80) { }
questions.explanation: else if adds another condition to the chain.

questions.question: What is printed when x is 7? if (x > 10) cout << "A"; else if (x > 5) cout << "B"; else cout << "C";
questions.explanation: 7 is greater than 5 but not greater than 10, so B is printed.

questions.question: Complete the condition: age >= 13 ______ age <= 19
questions.explanation: Both comparisons need to be true, so logical AND is used.

questions.question: Which statement selects among multiple cases based on an expression?
questions.explanation: switch selects a case based on the value of an expression.

flashcards.title: else if

flashcards.title: Nested Condition
flashcards.definition: A conditional placed inside another conditional block.

flashcards.title: switch
flashcards.definition: Selects code based on matching case labels.

questions.question: What happens when a switch case has no break?
choices: Execution may fall through to the next case
questions.explanation: Without break, execution continues into subsequent cases unless another control flow statement stops it.

questions.question: Complete the switch case: case 1: std::cout << "One"; ______;
questions.explanation: break prevents execution from falling through to later cases.

questions.question: Which branch handles the situation where no switch case matches?
questions.explanation: default handles unmatched switch cases.

questions.question: Complete the fallback branch: switch (choice) { ______: std::cout << "Invalid"; }
questions.explanation: default provides code for values that do not match a case.

questions.question: Which operator provides short-circuit logical AND?
questions.explanation: && performs logical AND with short-circuit evaluation.

flashcards.title: default
flashcards.definition: The switch branch used when no case matches.

flashcards.title: Fall-Through
flashcards.definition: Execution continuing into a following switch case.

flashcards.title: Short-Circuit AND
flashcards.definition: Stops evaluating when the left side is false.

questions.question: Which loop is commonly used with a counter?
questions.explanation: for loops conveniently contain initialization, condition, and update.

questions.question: Complete the loop: ______ (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { }
questions.explanation: for starts a counter-controlled loop.

questions.question: How many times does for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) execute?
questions.explanation: The loop runs with i equal to 0, 1, 2, and 3.

questions.question: Complete the update expression: for (int i = 0; i < 5; i______)
questions.explanation: ++ increments i by one.

questions.question: Which keyword immediately exits a loop?
questions.explanation: break exits the nearest loop.

flashcards.title: for Loop
flashcards.definition: A loop with initialization, condition, and update sections.

flashcards.title: Loop Counter
flashcards.definition: A variable used to track loop iterations.

flashcards.title: break
flashcards.definition: Immediately exits the nearest loop.

questions.question: Which loop checks its condition before each iteration?
questions.explanation: while checks its condition before executing the body.

questions.question: Complete the loop: ______ (count > 0) { count--; }
questions.explanation: while repeats while count is greater than zero.

questions.question: Which keyword skips the rest of the current iteration?
questions.explanation: continue proceeds to the next iteration.

questions.question: Complete the statement: ______; // skip remaining statements
questions.explanation: continue skips the remainder of the current loop iteration.

questions.question: Which loop executes its body at least once?
questions.explanation: do-while executes its body before checking its condition.

flashcards.title: while
flashcards.definition: Repeats while a condition is true.

flashcards.title: continue
flashcards.definition: Skips to the next loop iteration.

flashcards.title: do-while
flashcards.definition: Runs its body before checking the condition.

questions.question: What does a range-based for loop iterate over?
questions.explanation: A range-based for loop directly iterates over elements of a range.

questions.question: Complete the nested loop update: for (int j = 0; j < 2; j______)
questions.explanation: ++ increments the inner loop counter.

questions.question: What can happen if a loop condition never becomes false?
questions.explanation: A loop whose condition stays true can execute indefinitely.

flashcards.title: Range-Based for

flashcards.title: Nested Loop
flashcards.definition: A loop located inside another loop.

flashcards.title: Infinite Loop
flashcards.definition: A loop that does not reach a terminating condition.

questions.question: What is a function?

questions.explanation: int is the return type because the function returns an integer.

questions.explanation: void indicates that a function does not return a value.

questions.explanation: The function prints text and does not return a value.

questions.question: What is a parameter?

questions.explanation: Parameters are named variables declared in a function's parameter list.

flashcards.title: Function

flashcards.syntax: int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }

flashcards.title: Parameter
flashcards.definition: A named input declared by a function.

flashcards.title: void
flashcards.definition: A return type indicating that no value is returned.

questions.question: What keyword sends a value back from a function?
questions.explanation: return ends the function and provides a value to the caller.

questions.explanation: return sends the square to the caller.

questions.explanation: A function prototype declares a function's signature before its definition.

questions.explanation: A function prototype ends with a semicolon.

questions.question: What does a default argument provide?

flashcards.title: return

flashcards.title: Function Prototype

flashcards.title: Default Argument
flashcards.definition: A fallback parameter value used when an argument is omitted.

questions.explanation: A reference parameter aliases the caller's object, allowing modifications to affect the original.

questions.explanation: The function calls itself with a smaller value.

questions.explanation: &value obtains the address of value.

questions.explanation: Unary * accesses the object referred to by a pointer.

Only an object outside the class
